rubrics: The response should produce enforcement letter 3 using the template provided in the prompt.
The response should mention the child's name is Graeme Sheen.
The response should contain the date of birth of Graeme Sheen: 18/12/2010.
The response should mention that Graeme Sheen has been absent from school 9 times without permission since 26/10/2025.
The response should address the letter to John Sheen.

The response should not fabricate information to fill in the blanks in the response, leaving it blank instead. For example, the response should not fabricate a school contact or an attendance percentage.
The response should conclude by mentioning any missing information not provided by the user that is necessary to complete the letter. For example, the attendance percentage or the school contact.
The response should not contain an introduction or any follow up questions.
The response should include the current date which is 27/11/2025.
The response should mention that Bradford Council will investigate and consider legal action.
The response should include a website link,  www.bradford.gov.uk/attendance,  containing information regarding  school attendance.

The response should include the legal citation and quote from Section 444 of the Education Act 1996. For example: ‘Section 444 of the Education Act 1996: “If a child of compulsory school age who is a registered pupil at a school fails to attend regularly, their parent is guilty of an offence.”’
The response should present the “Name of Child” and “DOB” line in the template format. For example: “Name of Child: Graeme Sheen DOB: 18/12/2010”.
The response should include an “Attendance Percentage: ” line.

The response should accurately interpret that the address at the beginning of the response should be the recipient's address. For example it should not state that the "school address" is missing in the missing information section at the end.
